subject: Quota alarm: Quicksave reserved throughput shortfall & latency spikes
messages:
From: Lucas Chen <lucas@quicksave.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Quicksave Engineering <ops@quicksave.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden 5xx spike and latency — reserved throughput not honoring commit

Aditya / Redwood team,

We started seeing a sharp uptick in 5xx responses and p95 latency for the Quicksave production tenant around 08:45 PST. Our dashboards show token generation timeouts and long tail latencies coinciding with sustained QPS that should be covered by our reserved capacity (contracted 1.2k QPS). The customer impact: two checkout services timed out for ~3 minutes and we saw ~0.7% error rate across the past 30 minutes.

Quick observations: 
- Graphs: CPU/GPU utilization on our side is normal; errors originate downstream from Redwood endpoints (5xx + 429 bursts).
- We were expecting automatic fallback to the dedicated pool variant — that didn’t happen.

This is urgent; our product is in a payment flow window and we need remediation now. Can you confirm whether the reserved throughput is being honored and what the immediate mitigation is?

Attached a short snippet of the 5xx traces.

Thanks,
Lucas
Sr. Ops Engineer, Quicksave
[Attachment: quicksave-error-samples.log (text)]

From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Quicksave Engineering <ops@quicksave.com>, Lucas Chen <lucas@quicksave.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Nov 2025 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx spike and latency — reserved throughput not honoring commit

Lucas — thanks for the heads up and for the log samples. I’m escalating to infra and request immediate telemetry + mitigation. Initial triage plan below: 

1) Irene (infra) to validate whether the dedicated GPU pool for Quicksave is saturated or if routing fell back incorrectly.
2) If saturation confirmed, we’ll push an emergency burst (short-term) and open a reserved-capacity adjustment with procurement.
3) Dylan / Sales will prepare exec authorization for any emergency credits / temporary capacity we need to allocate.

Irene — can you confirm observed evictions, queue depths, and whether the reserved QPS token allocator is reporting quota exhaustion?

Lucas — we’ll aim to provide a 30-minute interim update. Apologies for the disruption; we’ll prioritize.

—Aditya
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Quicksave Engineering <ops@quicksave.com>, Lucas Chen <lucas@quicksave.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Nov 2025 09:36:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx spike and latency — reserved throughput not honoring commit

Quick triage notes (what I see):
- Time window: 08:40–09:05 PST: dedicated pool for Quicksave shows sustained queue length increase; scheduling backlog on GPU hosts (nvlink hops) rose ~3.6x.
- Allocator state: reserved token bucket hit hard at 1.2k QPS; fallback routing attempted but the fallback pool was itself constrained because of a concurrent cross-tenant surge on the same host group.
- Error signatures: 503s tied to inference worker rejection (queue overflow) and 429s from token-throttler. Not an upstream network issue.

Immediate mitigations executed at 09:30 PST:
- Applied emergency burst config: +600 QPS to Quicksave routed to alternate host group (24h temporary).
- Increased per-request timeout knob to avoid noisy retries (client-side recommended).
- Eviction policy relaxed briefly to allow in-flight KV-cache warmups.

Next steps (24–72h):
- We propose a temporary dedicated buffer (600 QPS) for the remainder of the week while we re-balance host allocations.
- Infra will provide a post-incident metrics pack (attached reserved-throughput-metrics-20251115.csv).

Open asks for Sales/Execs: 
- Authorization for the 24h emergency burst (costs and contract change) and approval for a credit to Quicksave for downtime.
- Procurement path to expand reserved capacity or move Quicksave to an isolated host group.

I’ll follow up with the metrics export and a brief runbook excerpt.

—Irene
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: reserved-throughput-metrics-20251115.csv (CSV)]

From: dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Quicksave Engineering <ops@quicksave.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Nov 2025 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx spike and latency — reserved throughput not honoring commit

Thanks Irene — solid breakdown. Marking this for exec approval. TL;DR for leadership: 

- Root issue: cross-tenant pressure on the host group that also backs Quicksave’s reserved pool caused allocator exhaustion and queued worker rejections.
- Immediate remediation: emergency +600 QPS burst applied; should reduce 503s and p95 in next 15–30m.
- Risk/ask: to make Quicksave whole and prevent repeat, we need either (A) an isolated host group (capex/ops time + contract amendment), or (B) a higher committed reservation (procurement + pricing adjustment).

Ask for Vivek / Marissa: please authorize the emergency burst charges (estimated incremental cost: ~$18k for 24h of additional GPU headroom) and pre-approve a one-time customer credit (I propose 25% of the Nov invoice as immediate remediation). We should also sign off on the mutual action plan (attached draft) to sequence host isolation or reservation increase.

If leadership prefers a faster procurement path, I can route the contract amendment to Legal today — otherwise Procurement/Finance will need to triage next steps Monday.

Lucas — apologies again; we’re monitoring and I’ll send a final update when infra confirms steady-state.

—Dylan
Director, Sales — Priority Accounts, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mutual-action-plan-draft.docx (DOCX)]

From: Lucas Chen <lucas@quicksave.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Quicksave Engineering <ops@quicksave.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Nov 2025 14:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx spike and latency — reserved throughput not honoring commit

Aditya / team — appreciate the rapid response and the emergency burst. After the burst was applied the error rate dropped to baseline and p95 improved by ~420ms over the prior window. 

Two asks from our side before we close the loop: 
1) A concrete timeline for moving Quicksave to an isolated host group (or an ETA for reservation increase to be provisioned).
2) A written confirmation of the credit and the exact billing adjustment for November.

If we can get a MAP and timeline by EOD Monday (Nov 17) that should be sufficient for our execs to avoid escalation. We’re happy to join a 30-minute sync Monday morning if that helps.

Thanks again — Lucas
Sr. Ops Engineer, Quicksave
